This is architecturally enforced via (a) prompt-level sequence constraints (manifest read is first in system prompt), (b) tool-gating (create-component tool forbidden unless retrieve-component was called first in this session), (c) decision-log requirement (intentional exceptions are logged, not silent violations).

keyFindings.insight: Manifest must be **compact, intent-indexed, and embeddings-dense** to achieve high recall in limited context windows. Structure as: `{id, intent-keywords, canonical-name, values, location, created-by, created-date, similarity-vector}` with optional semantic fingerprint (hash of source/behavior, not just name). A 200–500-component design system should compress into <50KB JSON, indexed by intent-clusters (spacing, color, button-types, etc.), enabling sub-100ms retrieval.
keyFindings.evidence: Dense Retrieval models and learned indexes (product quantization, tree-based indexing) yield significant latency/memory improvements. Microsoft Azure AI Search agentic retrieval and semantic caching systems (embedding-based similarity in Kong AI Gateway) show that compact, multi-indexed structures support both dense vector search and keyword-driven lookup. Semantic similarity thresholds of 0.5–0.8 are standard; 0.1–0.2 for strict matching.
keyFindings.implication: Manifest is NOT human-readable prose documentation; it is a machine-optimized index with human-readable tags as secondary keys. Include both dense vectors (from component source code/behavior) and sparse keyword indices (intent, variant, platform). Generate embedding fingerprint deterministically from source (hash(code)) so two agents naming the same concept produce identical IDs and vectors, enabling automatic deduplication.

keyFindings.insight: **Deterministic ID and naming** prevent the orphan-component and collision problem. Generate component IDs as `hash(intent + signature + platform)` deterministically, not uuid(); two agents creating a 'primary button' independently should compute the same ID. Naming follows template: `{category}/{variant}/{modifiers}` (e.g., `button/primary/large-solid`, `spacing/xs`, `color/surface/light`). Disallow free-form naming; require template selection from taxonomy.
keyFindings.evidence: Prior art on semantic naming through generation shows templates enable language compression without meaning loss. Stateless Snowflake ID generation and deterministic logic synthesis algorithms show that identity derived from input content (not creation order) prevents collisions and enables reproducibility. Claude Code plugin naming conventions (tier prefixes, slug-based IDs) operationalize deterministic ID as convention-level enforcement.
keyFindings.implication: Component ID should be a content-hash derivative, not a sequential or random value. Implement as: `id = sha256(hash(intent_keyword + signature_fingerprint + platform))[:16]`. Two agents independently creating a 'primary button with 48px height' will generate the same ID; the second agent's create tool detects collision and merges rather than diverging. Naming template must be enforced by dropdown/enum, not free-form input.

keyFindings.insight: **Similarity threshold + closest-existing-match rule** operationalizes reuse-vs-create decisions. Compute cosine similarity between new intent-embedding and all manifest entries; if max-similarity >= threshold (recommend 0.78 for design systems, tunable per org), reuse + adapt the closest match rather than create new. Log the decision: matched-to ID, similarity score, adaptation (if any). If similarity < threshold, create as net-new, but require justification in decision log (why existing closest match insufficient).
keyFindings.evidence: Semantic caching in Kong AI Gateway and ensemble embedding approaches show threshold tuning trades recall vs. precision; 0.75–0.85 balances false positives vs. false negatives in practice. Optimal threshold depends on embedding model dimensionality and data variation. Score distributions (not single scores) improve robustness by capturing margin of confidence. Decision logging is critical for compliance and re-training.
keyFindings.implication: Implement similarity scorer as: (1) embed new intent using same model as manifest (deterministic), (2) compute cosine similarity to all manifest entries, (3) rank by score, (4) if top-1 >= 0.78, return reuse recommendation + closest ID; else propose creation. Log all decisions (reuse/create, matched-to-id, score) in decision.log. Expose threshold tuning via config; default 0.78.

keyFindings.insight: **Register-after-create loop** prevents orphan components and ensures manifest freshness. When an agent creates a new component/token: (1) auto-generate ID deterministically, (2) extract intent keywords (LLM-parsed from task description), (3) compute embedding fingerprint from source, (4) append to manifest with metadata (agent-id, timestamp, source-location, status='NEW'), (5) regenerate manifest indices (keyword-to-id, semantic vector-index). Do NOT require manual registration; make it automatic post-creation, but require confirmation before committing to repo.
keyFindings.evidence: Audit trails in RAG systems (tamper-proof append-only logs, WORM storage) and decision-log patterns show that logging decisions post-facto (not just pre-facto) enables accountability and traceability. Versioning that ties embeddings, index snapshots, and prompt text together supports rollback and auditability (cited in RAG compliance frameworks).
keyFindings.implication: Create tool emits: (code, manifest-entry-draft, decision-log-entry). Agent prompts user: 'Created new PrimaryButton at {location}. Ready to register? Manifest entry: {json}.' User confirms; agent appends and rebuilds indices. This workflow ensures no created component is invisible; if user rejects registration, creation is rolled back or marked as experimental.

keyFindings.insight: **Decision logs for intentional exceptions** are essential for preventing future re-invention of deliberate off-spec choices. Log format: `{date, decision-id, component-id, intent, exception-type (off-scale-value | extra-variant | platform-specific), justification, decision-maker, status (active | resolved)}`. Query decision log before proposing refactors; if a value is off-scale but logged as intentional, surface the reason rather than 'fixing' it. This turns a version-control nightmare into a feature.
keyFindings.evidence: Compliance and audit frameworks require explicit decision recording (user identity, timestamp, evidence, decision text). Decision-log patterns enable post-hoc reasoning: auditors and future agents understand *why* an inconsistency exists, not just that it does. This is critical for long-lived codebases where 'inconsistency' is often technical debt or intentional platform-specific logic.
keyFindings.implication: Decision log is a first-class artifact (decision-log.json), not hidden in commit messages. Structure: array of entries with decision-id (deterministic), component-id, justification, status. Agents must query decision log before proposing refactors; if found, propose with note: 'This was logged as intentional on [date] because [justification]. Update decision status or override?'

keyFindings.insight: **Make raw literals and orphan components architecturally awkward** through linting gates and tool gating, not just convention. Implement: (1) pre-commit hook that scans for numeric literals in layout/styling positions and rejects if not in decision log; (2) forbid create-component tool unless manifest was read (detect via tool-call order in session); (3) linter rule: any View/Style/Modifier not referenced in manifest.json triggers error; (4) CI gate: no new components unless registered and cross-linked in design system namespace.
keyFindings.evidence: Native enforcement points (style protocols, ViewModifier extraction, Environment cascading) make consistent paths ergonomic in SwiftUI. Memento-Skills and skill-rewrite frameworks show that external memory (structured markdown, JSON manifest) is necessary but insufficient; the *prompt* and *tool-gating* must operationalize retrieval and reuse.
keyFindings.implication: Linting is not post-hoc quality; it is pre-creation friction. Build pre-commit hooks that detect numeric literals in layout contexts (padding, frame, cornerRadius, fontSize) and require DS.* token references. Add CI gate: manifest-coverage linter ensures all components in codebase appear in manifest; missing entry → build failure with 'Register this component' prompt.

keyFindings.insight: **Manifest-presentation format for cross-agent recall**: Use a hybrid structure combining dense-vector indexing, keyword tagging, and semantic hashing. Example: `{components: [{id (deterministic), name, intent-keywords (array), category, variants (enum), values ({ token-name: value }), platform, created-by, created-date, source-location, status, embedding-fingerprint, decision-log-references}], indices: {by-category, by-intent, by-platform, semantic-vector-index}, decision-log-references (array of decision-ids)}`. Keep JSON size <50KB by storing embedding fingerprints (32-char hash) not full vectors.
keyFindings.evidence: MCP servers (shadcn/ui MCP, Synergy design system MCP, design-systems-mcp) expose components via structured metadata queries. Azure AI Search agentic retrieval and dense-retrieval models show that multi-indexing (by category, platform, intent) enables fast sub-second queries. Learned indexes with cardinality support show KB-scale index overhead.
keyFindings.implication: Manifest is a single JSON file with three sections: (1) components array (core catalog), (2) indices object (pre-computed keyword, category, platform, and semantic-vector lookup), (3) metadata (schema version, last-updated, decision-log-refs). Do not version-control embedding vectors; compute on-the-fly from source at index-rebuild time. Provide manifest-query tool (part of framework harness) for agents to retrieve candidates in <100ms.

keyFindings.insight: **System prompt sequence** must enforce retrieval-before-creation as a **required operational step**, not a suggestion. Template: (1) 'You MUST read the current manifest before proposing any component creation.' (2) 'Query the manifest for existing components matching intent: [intent]. Score each by similarity (0.0–1.0). If max-similarity >= 0.78, REUSE the closest match and justify any adaptation.' (3) 'Only if no suitable match exists, create new. Assign deterministic ID, register to manifest, log decision.' (4) 'All exceptions must be logged in decision-log with justification.' (5) 'Output: {code, manifest-entries (new or none), decision-log-entries (if applicable)}.' This sequence is structural, not advisory.
keyFindings.evidence: ARCS (synthesize-execute-repair) and RepoAI (intent classification + multi-agent coordination) show that explicit ordering and sequential constraints in agentic prompts drive convergence. Memento-Skills and mem0 systems use hierarchical write-manage-read loops as the operational core. Hierarchical agent memory (G-Memory) uses explicit graph traversal and multi-level retrieval as the control structure.
keyFindings.implication: System prompt is not a preamble; it is a **protocol specification**. Use numbered steps, explicit gates ('MUST read manifest before proposing creation'), and tool-call dependencies (create-tool requires prior call to query-manifest-tool). This is enforced in prompt structure, not via user instructions.

keyFindings.insight: **Cross-agent deduplication and merge** require consensus on ID and similarity. When agent-A creates component ID 'button/primary/48' and agent-B independently computes the same ID (via deterministic hashing), the framework detects collision via ID-index lookup and proposes merge: 'button/primary/48 exists (created by agent-A). Your version differs: [diff]. Merge, update source-location to [both agents], or create variant?' This turns independent creation into collaborative convergence.
keyFindings.evidence: MemAdapter (fast alignment across agent memory paradigms via generative subgraph retrieval) and G-Memory (bi-directional memory traversal, selective sharing) show that explicit merge and conflict-resolution at the memory level enable multi-agent coherence. Deterministic ID generation (content-hash) prevents collision fragmentation.
keyFindings.implication: Implement collision detection at registration time: before appending component to manifest, hash(intent + signature) to compute ID. Query manifest ID-index for collision. If found, diff source and metadata; propose merge (union of both source-locations), flag for review, or reject creation (user confirms either merge or variant).

keyFindings.insight: **Manifest-query tool** as a first-class agent capability: expose manifest retrieval as a callable tool (parallel to create-component, refactor-code, etc.), not just embedded in system prompt. Tool interface: `query-manifest({intent: string, category?: string, platform?: string, limit?: 5}) -> [{id, name, similarity-score, values, source-location, decision-log-refs}]`. Agents call this explicitly before proposing creation; tool enforces the retrieve-first protocol. Log all queries in manifest-access.log for observability.
keyFindings.evidence: MCP servers provide tool-based access to external context (shadcn/ui search, design-system-mcp queries). Azure AI Search exposes agentic retrieval as callable endpoints. Design system MCP patterns show that tool-based manifest access is more maintainable than embedding entire catalog in prompt.
keyFindings.implication: Framework harness includes manifest-query tool (built on manifest JSON, with embedding-based semantic search and keyword indexing). Agents call it: result instructs next action (reuse, adapt, or create). Tool output includes similarity scores and justification, supporting transparent decision-making.

recommendationsForFramework: Implement mandatory retrieve-before-create as tool-call sequencing: create-component tool is forbidden unless query-manifest-tool was called first in this session. Enforce in framework harness (tool-call validator).

Build hybrid manifest structure (JSON): {components[], indices{by-category, by-intent, by-platform, semantic-vectors}, decision-logs{array}}. Keep total size <50KB; store embedding fingerprints (sha256 hashes) not full vectors. Regenerate vectors on index-rebuild from source.

Generate component IDs deterministically as sha256(intent-keyword + behavior-signature + platform)[:16]. Two agents creating the same logical component independently will compute identical IDs; collision detection enables merge, not fragmentation.

Set similarity threshold for reuse-vs-create at 0.78 (configurable). If top manifest match >= 0.78, REUSE (with adaptation if needed) and log decision (matched-to-id, similarity-score). If <0.78, create new but require justification in decision-log.

Auto-register all new components post-creation: extract intent from task, compute deterministic ID, snapshot source location, append to manifest.json with metadata (agent-id, timestamp, status='NEW'). Require user confirmation before committing; never silent orphan creation.

Operationalize decision-log as first-class artifact (decision-log.json): {date, decision-id, component-id, intent, exception-type, justification, decision-maker, status}. Query decision-log before refactoring; if intentional exception logged, surface reason rather than auto-fixing.

Add pre-commit linting hooks: (1) reject numeric literals in layout/style positions unless referenced in DS.* tokens; (2) scan for orphan components (in codebase but not in manifest); (3) verify all manifest entries are actually used (cross-reference). Fail build if violations found.

Expose manifest-query tool as a first-class agent capability: query-manifest({intent, category?, platform?, limit?}) returns [{id, name, similarity, values, source-location}]. Log all queries in manifest-access.log for observability and to debug retrieval failures.

System prompt operationalizes retrieval as a mandatory protocol: 'Step 1: Read manifest. Step 2: Query-manifest for intent matches, score by similarity. Step 3: If max-similarity >= 0.78, REUSE; else create. Step 4: Log decision (reuse-to-id / create-new). Step 5: Register post-creation.' This is not advice; it is the operational sequence.

Implement collision detection at registration: hash(intent + signature) to compute ID before appending to manifest. If ID exists in manifest, diff source and metadata; propose merge (union both locations), variant (new ID with different signature), or reject. Enable multi-agent convergence via explicit merge, not silent fragmentation.

Design manifest query to support both semantic (embedding-based) and keyword-based retrieval: index by (category, intent-keywords, platform, author). Support queries like 'find buttons with height ~48' and 'find spacing tokens < 16'. Expose as structured query language (simple DSL), not just vector search.

Add intent-fingerprinting to manifest entries: {intent-hash, intent-keywords[], intent-description}. When agent proposes new component, parse intent from task description (LLM-assisted), compute fingerprint, query manifest by intent-hash for collisions. This catches near-duplicates that semantic similarity alone might miss.

Create a framework harness (Node.js/Python CLI or TypeScript module) that encapsulates: (1) manifest loader/validator, (2) manifest-query tool (semantic + keyword), (3) ID generator (deterministic hash), (4) collision detector, (5) decision-log query, (6) linting rules (numeric-literal, orphan-component, cross-reference), (7) registration workflow. This harness is the single source of truth for all agents.

Provide exemplar decision-log entries and exception justifications (template library): 'platform-specific-override', 'temporary-workaround-bug-XYZ', 'legacy-compatibility', 'performance-optimization-measured-at-XYZ'. Agents copy template, fill reason; non-template exceptions require review.

Implement CI/CD gate: manifest-coverage linter ensures all components in codebase appear in manifest.json. Missing entry causes build failure with prompt: 'Component {name} at {location} not in manifest. Register it? [Auto-register button] [Ignore (add to exception-list)].' Never allow builds with orphan components.

Manifest versioning: include schema-version, last-updated timestamp, agent-id of last updater, git-commit-hash. This supports rollback and auditability. All manifest changes are tracked in version-control; decision-log changes too. Enable 'what changed in the design system' queries.

For multi-platform systems (web + iOS + Android): partition manifest entries by platform but allow cross-platform queries (intent matching across platform boundaries). When agent finds similar component on different platform, expose as reuse-opportunity-with-adaptation ('this button pattern exists for web; adapt for iOS?').

Expose manifest diff tool: compare-manifest(manifest-v1, manifest-v2) returns {components-added, components-removed, components-modified, entries-added-to-decision-log}. Use this for design-system release notes and to surface drift/consolidation opportunities.

Build human-facing manifest dashboard: list all components, group by category/platform, show decision-log entries, visualize similarity clusters (components near threshold), expose missing-coverage warnings. This is observability for design system health, not just technical artifact.
pitfalls: Making manifest read optional or a 'nice-to-have' in system prompt. Agents will skip it under time pressure; make it tool-call sequencing that hard-gates creation (create-tool forbidden until query-manifest called). Soft guidance fails.

Storing full embedding vectors in manifest JSON. Vectors bloat file size (5–10MB for 500 components with 1536-dim embeddings). Instead, store fingerprints (hashes); regenerate vectors from source at index time. Trade: slower first query, persistent efficiency.

Using UUID or random IDs for components. Two agents creating the same logical component independently will get different IDs, fragmenting the catalog. Use deterministic content-hashing; collisions become merge opportunities, not blind duplication.

Setting similarity threshold too high (>0.9). You'll reject many valid reuse opportunities; agents revert to creating variants. Too low (<0.6), you reuse inappropriately and create false positive merges. Sweet spot for design systems: 0.75–0.82, tuned empirically on real intent clusters.

Leaving decision-log queries optional. Agents will see 'off-spec value' and auto-refactor without checking if it was intentional. Always query decision-log before proposing refactors; surface reason if logged exception found. This prevents the 'why did my workaround get deleted' trap.

Manual registration post-creation. Agents (and developers) forget; components become orphans in code but absent from manifest. Auto-register all new components; require user confirmation but make the default 'register.' This flips the incentive structure.

Free-form component naming. Names drift, become inconsistent, and are unsearchable. Use deterministic naming templates (category/variant/modifiers), enforced by dropdown/enum. Disallow free-form input.

Not logging manifest queries. Without visibility into what agents are searching for, you can't diagnose retrieval failures (bad intent keywords in manifest, embedding model mismatch, etc.). Log all queries (intent, returned candidates, agent-id, timestamp); use for observability.

Storing decision-log only in commit messages. Hard to query programmatically; agents can't access it at runtime. Make decision-log a first-class JSON file, queryable by agent via decision-log-query tool.

Ignoring platform differences in multi-platform systems. Web and iOS components have different constraints; forcing reuse across platform boundaries creates Frankenstein designs. Partition manifest by platform; allow cross-platform queries as 'reuse with adaptation' suggestions, not hard merges.

Building manifest-query without keyword indexing. Semantic search alone misses intent-level queries ('find spacing tokens <16', 'find buttons with large variant'). Use hybrid search: keyword + semantic. Keyword-first for exact matches, semantic for fuzzy intent matching.

Assuming agents will understand intent from task description alone. Parse intent explicitly (LLM-assisted), extract keywords, compute fingerprint, store in manifest. This makes intent queryable and enables intent-collision detection.

Not versioning manifest or decision-log. Can't audit drift, roll back bad merges, or answer 'what changed in the design system?' Make manifest part of version control; track all changes as commits with metadata.

Making linting warnings, not errors. Developers ignore warnings. Use hard pre-commit gates: numeric literals in layout positions → build failure. Orphan components → build failure. Unregistered component → build failure. Make consistency the path of least resistance.

Exposing raw embeddings or similarity scores without justification. Agents and humans don't know why a match was returned. Always return {candidate-id, name, similarity-score, matched-intent-keywords, why-matched (human-readable)}. Transparency builds trust in retrieval.

Building manifest for humans first, machines second. Manifest should be machine-optimized (compact, indexed, queryable); human readability is secondary. Use tools to render manifests as dashboards for humans; don't bloat the data structure with prose.

Not detecting/resolving ID collisions at registration time. Two agents create the same component independently, both register, you get fragmented IDs. Always check ID-index for collisions before appending; propose merge or variant.

Assuming semantic similarity alone solves deduplication. Similarity is noisy; intent-level deduplication (fingerprinting, keyword collision) catches more duplicates. Use multi-level deduplication: hash-based (intent fingerprint), semantic (embedding similarity), keyword (tag intersection).

brief.problemModel:
AI UI drift is NOT primarily a taste failure or a hallucination problem — it is a RETRIEVAL and STATE failure that masquerades as taste. Decompose every divergence into three orthogonal causes, each with a distinct fix:

(1) RETRIEVAL FAILURE (the dominant cause, ~70% of drift): The model never had the relevant fact in context. Tokens, existing components, and naming precedents are not retrievable because they were never loaded — task context fills the window first. Result: re-invention of `Button.tsx` vs `PrimaryButton.tsx`, or padding 16 emitted as a literal because the token was never visible. Fix = retrieval architecture (queryable manifest + mandatory retrieve-before-create). Larger context windows do NOT fix this; they defer it.

(2) STATELESS RE-INVENTION (cross-session): Each API call is a fresh inference with zero memory of prior calls. Button v1 (radius 6) at 11am and Button v2 (radius 8) at 2pm are mutually unaware. Fix = external persistent state (a Git-tracked manifest the agent queries every session). Prompting "be consistent" is performative without queryable prior state.

(3) SAMPLING VARIANCE (in-session, temperature>0): 15px vs 16px, #F0F0F0 vs #F5F5F5 are token-selection randomness, not decisions. Fix = temperature 0.0–0.2 for UI code + multi-sample consensus for high-stakes components.

TASTE vs RETRIEVAL is the load-bearing distinction. TASTE = choosing 12px from a valid range when no prior decision exists (legitimately free; resolve ONCE at the system/token level, then it stops being taste). RETRIEVAL = choosing 12px, then 16px for the same role without checking what was chosen before (a fact was omitted that existed). Conflating these produces the canonical wrong fix: bloating prompts with "be consistent and tasteful" exhortations that address neither the missing index nor the missing state. The framework's job is to collapse taste into a finite set of pre-made decisions (tokens + components + variants-as-enums) so that at generation time there is nothing left to taste — only facts to retrieve. Hardcoded literals are then revealed as cost-optimized outputs of a system that failed to make the token cheaper to emit than the literal.
brief.coreThesis: Design consistency is a retrieval-and-state problem disguised as a taste problem: make the right value cheaper to retrieve than to invent, persist every decision in one machine-queryable manifest that spans web and SwiftUI, gate creation behind mandatory retrieval, and the same independent agents will converge on the same UI — which a four-part composite score then proves.

frameworkPillars.name: One manifest, two emitters (single source of truth)
frameworkPillars.rationale: Cross-session and cross-stack drift both stem from the absence of shared external state. A platform-agnostic manifest is the only artifact that lets a React agent and a SwiftUI agent reuse the SAME decisions. It must be machine-optimized (queryable, indexed) first and human-readable second — prose specs exhaust the context window and are unparseable.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: A single DTCG-superset JSON (`design-system.json`) holds primitives→semantic→component token layers plus a component registry. Platform transform rules live as DATA (not code) inside the manifest: web→[name/kebab, color/hex, dimension/rem]→CSS vars + Tailwind @theme + TS types; swift→[name/camelCase enum-static, color/AssetCatalog, dimension/CGFloat]→`DS.swift` enum + `.xcassets`. WEB: tokens resolve to `var(--color-action-primary)` / Tailwind `@theme` utilities; components resolve to a shadcn-style registry-item. SWIFT: scalar tokens→`enum DS.Spacing { static let md: CGFloat = 16 }`, semantic colors→Asset Catalog ColorSet + `extension ShapeStyle where Self == Color`, cascading values (theme/density)→`@Entry` EnvironmentValues, component variants→`ButtonStyle` with an enum Variant. Codegen output is gitignored; the JSON is the source. CI regenerates and validates all platform outputs from the JSON on every change.

frameworkPillars.name: Retrieve-before-create, structurally enforced
frameworkPillars.rationale: Soft guidance ('reuse existing components') fails under task pressure — agents revert to invention. Retrieval must be a hard precondition, not a courtesy. This is the single highest-leverage convergence mechanism: it eliminates synonym bloat (Card/CardWrapper/c-card) by forcing a similarity check before any new artifact exists.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: A `query_manifest({intent, category?, platform?, limit?})` tool is a first-class capability. The harness tool-call validator FORBIDS `create_component` unless `query_manifest` was called earlier in the same session. WEB: query returns existing registry items with import paths, props, anti-patterns, and token requirements to paste as reference. SWIFT: query returns existing ViewModifiers/Styles/DS tokens with source locations. If top match ≥ 0.78 cosine similarity → REUSE/adapt and log the match; if < 0.78 → create new, but only as a registered, first-class artifact (never an inline special case), with a justification logged.

frameworkPillars.name: Mechanical constraint over exhortation
frameworkPillars.rationale: Literals are emitted because nothing forbade them and they were cheaper than tokens. Consistency must be the path of least resistance and deviation must be awkward. 'Be consistent' is a no-op; a lint gate that fails the build is not.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: Hard system-prompt constraints: 'NEVER emit raw px/hex/shadow/font-size literals; reference tokens only; if no token exists, ask before generating.' Generation config pinned to temperature 0.1–0.2 (0.0 for token/color name references). Variants modeled as ENUMS, not free parameters, on BOTH stacks (React discriminated-union `variant` prop; SwiftUI `enum Variant`) so there is no arbitrary-size argument to pass. Post-generation lint gates: WEB = stylelint-declaration-strict-value + an ESLint token-adherence rule (reject literal px/hex in style positions); SWIFT = SwiftLint `no_magic_numbers` + custom_rules regex banning `padding(\d+)`, `cornerRadius(\d+)`, `Color\.(red|blue|green)`, `.font(.system(size:`. Pre-commit + CI fail on violations not present in the decision log.

frameworkPillars.name: Register-after-create + decision log (no orphans, no silent fixes)
frameworkPillars.rationale: A created component invisible to the manifest is re-invented next session — the orphan problem. And an intentional off-scale value silently 'fixed' by a later audit is the 'why did my workaround get deleted' trap. Both are solved by making registration automatic and exceptions first-class.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: On create: deterministically compute `id = sha256(intent_keywords + signature_fingerprint + platform)[:16]`, extract intent keywords, append to manifest with metadata (agent-id, timestamp, source-location, status='NEW'), rebuild indices, then require user confirmation before commit. Two agents independently building 'primary button 48px' compute the SAME id → collision detected at registration → propose merge, not fork. Intentional exceptions go in `decision-log.json` ({decision-id, component-id, exception-type, justification, status}); the audit/refactor path MUST query it before proposing any change and surface the logged reason instead of auto-fixing.

frameworkPillars.name: Measurable convergence (the score closes the loop)
frameworkPillars.rationale: A consistency framework that cannot be measured cannot be tuned or trusted. The composite score is both the acceptance test for the harness and the longitudinal drift detector in CI — it turns 'looks consistent' into a number that gates merges and proves the framework works across the two stacks.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: Four AST-based sub-metrics (token-adherence, component-reuse, value-clustering, cross-session convergence) computed by stack-specific parsers — Babel/@babel/parser + postcss for React/CSS/Tailwind, SwiftSyntax for SwiftUI — compared against the same manifest. Sub-scores reported separately (radar chart) plus a single 0–100 composite. Any sub-score < 60 is flagged regardless of composite. CI gate fails merges below threshold (default 75) and emits remediation hints ('replace padding(16) with DS.Spacing.md').

brief.manifestDesign:
SINGLE FILE: `design-system.json`. DTCG-superset (uses `$value`/`$type`/`$description`, curly-brace refs `{group.token}`), extended with a component registry, platform transforms, indices, and metadata. This is the ONE source of truth both stacks and the scorer read.

TOP-LEVEL SHAPE:
{
  "$schema": "...", "manifestVersion": "1.0", "metadata": {version, lastUpdated, lastUpdatedBy, gitCommit, sourceOfTruthUrl, namingConvention},
  "tokens": { "primitives": {...}, "semantic": {...}, "composite": {...}, "component": {...} },
  "components": [ ...registry entries... ],
  "platforms": { "web": {transforms:[...], target:"css-vars|tailwind-v4"}, "swift": {transforms:[...], target:"enum+assetcatalog"} },
  "indices": { "byCategory": {...}, "byIntent": {...}, "byPlatform": {...}, "semanticVectors": {tokenId: "sha256-fingerprint"} },
  "decisionLog": [ ...exceptions... ]
}

TOKEN LAYERING (3 tiers + composites, refs enforced one-directionally):
- primitives: raw brand-agnostic values, NO refs. e.g. `"blue-500": {"$value":"#0066cc","$type":"color","$description":"Raw brand blue"}`, `"space-4":{"$value":"16px","$type":"dimension"}`.
- semantic: role-based, MUST ref a primitive (parser REJECTS semantic→semantic refs to forbid hidden layers). e.g. `"color.action.primary":{"$value":"{blue-500}","$type":"color","$description":"Primary interactive surface; must hit WCAG AA on color.bg.surface"}`.
- composite: ONE token with object $value (typography{fontFamily,fontSize,fontWeight,lineHeight,letterSpacing}, border{color,width,style}, shadow{x,y,blur,spread,color}). Sub-values MUST be refs, not hardcoded (shadow.color:{color.shadow.default}, never #000).
- component: component-scoped, refs semantic/composite only. e.g. `"button.primary.background":{"$value":"{color.action.primary}"}`.
$description answers WHY/WHERE, never restates the name (reject tautologies like 'primary primary color').

COMPONENT REGISTRY ENTRY (extends shadcn registry-item with the agentic fields existing systems lack — purpose, anti-patterns, relationships, when-to-use, a11y, tokenMap). Minimum required fields the validator enforces: id, canonicalName, purposeStatement, variants, antiPatterns, importOrSource, tokenMap. Full entry:
{
  "id": "sha256(intent+signature+platform)[:16]",
  "canonicalName": "Button", "intentKeywords": ["action","submit","cta"],
  "category": "button/primary",                          // template {category}/{variant}/{modifiers}, NOT free-form
  "purposeStatement": "Triggers an action; NOT navigation (use Link).",  // semantic intent, not a label
  "whenToUse": [{scenario, code, preferredComponent, whyNotAlternative}],
  "variants": [{name:"variant", values:["primary","secondary","danger"], type:"enum"}],
  "variantCombinations": {"invalid":[{"disabled":true,"loading":true}]},  // interaction matrix
  "antiPatterns": [{pattern:"two primary buttons side-by-side", reason, correctAlternative, severity:"must-not|should-not|deprecated"}],
  "relationships": {parentContexts:[...], incompatibleWith:[ids], requiredNeighbors:[...]},
  "a11y": [{attribute, value, required, variants}],
  "tokenMap": {"primary": ["button.primary.background","spacing.inset.md","radius.sm"]},  // tokens each variant requires
  "platform": "web|swift",
  "web": {importPath:"@/components/ui/button", files:[{path,type}], cssVars:{...}},
  "swift": {source:"DS/Buttons.swift:48", style:"DSButtonStyle", construct:"DSButton(...)"},
  "createdBy", "createdDate", "status":"stable|new|experimental|deprecated",
  "embeddingFingerprint": "sha256(...)",                 // hash, NOT full vector (keeps file <50KB)
  "decisionLogRefs": [decision-ids]
}

WEB MAPPING: tokens → CSS custom properties (`--color-action-primary`) AND/OR Tailwind v4 `@theme` (auto-utilities), plus TS type export; components → registry items consumed via MCP/import. SWIFT MAPPING: scalar tokens → `enum DS.Spacing { static let md: CGFloat = 16 }`; semantic colors → Asset Catalog ColorSet (Any+Dark appearances, auto dark-mode) surfaced via `extension ShapeStyle where Self == Color { static var dsActionPrimary }`; cascading tokens (theme/density) → `@Entry var dsTheme` in EnvironmentValues; component variants → `ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle` with `enum Variant`. Codegen (Style Dictionary / SwiftTokenGen) emits both targets from this JSON; generated code is gitignored, the JSON is canonical, CI asserts generated==manifest. VALIDATION (eager, at parse time before any codegen): every token has $type+$value; all refs resolve; no circular refs; composites have required sub-keys; semantic refs only primitives; component refs only semantic/composite; names match declared convention; every component has the minimum required fields.
brief.metricDesign:
COMPOSITE = 0.40·TA + 0.30·CR + 0.20·(VC·100) + 0.10·(CC·100), single 0–100. Default weights; tunable per org (token-critical → TA 50–60; reliability-critical → CC 20–25; document rationale). Report all four sub-scores separately; flag any sub-score < 60 even if composite passes. Tiers: 0–50 poor, 50–75 developing, 75–90 mature, 90–100 excellent. Toolchain: React/CSS via @babel/parser + @babel/traverse + postcss/postcss-scss (already in harness deps); SwiftUI via SwiftSyntax; all compared to the same `design-system.json`. Canonicalize values before any comparison (#FF0000=rgb(255,0,0)=red→lowercase hex; padding(16)=.padding(16)=padding(.md); aggressive whitespace/identifier normalization).

(1) TOKEN-ADHERENCE (TA), 0–100, weight 0.40:
  TA = (token_references / styleable_declarations) × 100.
  DENOMINATOR = every declaration where a token COULD apply: color, background, border-color, spacing (padding/margin/gap), font-size, font-weight, line-height, border-radius, box-shadow, transition, plus SwiftUI padding/frame/cornerRadius/foregroundStyle/font.
  NUMERATOR = declarations referencing a DEFINED manifest token (`var(--…)`, Tailwind token-utility, `DS.Spacing.md`, `.dsActionPrimary`). Raw literals that match no token = numerator 0.
  EXCLUDED from denominator (documented ruleset): `auto`, `0`, `inherit`, `currentColor`, unitless z-index/flex/opacity, vendor prefixes.
  TYPE-CHECK GUARD (closes the 'spacing token used for a color' false-pass): a reference only counts if its token $type matches the property family (color prop must ref color token, spacing prop must ref dimension token). Mismatch counts as a violation.

(2) COMPONENT-REUSE (CR), 0–100, weight 0.30:
  CR = (reused_instances + variation_reuses) / (total_instances + missed_opportunities) × 100.
  reused_instances = JSX elements / SwiftUI Views matching a registered component name. variation_reuses = same base component + explicit registered overrides (NOT penalized — intentional variants are fine). missed_opportunities = clone-detected groups: 3+ instances with near-identical AST structure (< 15% tree-edit distance) that are NOT a registered component (the synonym-bloat signal). Use semantic similarity (prop signature + behavior), not string match, to avoid false clone flags. Requires manifest component inventory as baseline.

(3) VALUE-CLUSTERING (VC), 0–1 (×100 in composite), weight 0.20:
  Per dimension d: efficiency_d = min(unique_values_observed_d, defined_tokens_d) / unique_values_observed_d. (If 5 spacing tokens defined and 12 distinct spacing values observed → 5/12 = 0.417.) Strip media-query/responsive variants and cluster by INTENT before counting (so responsive 16px-mobile/24px-desktop is not double-penalized).
  VC = weighted avg across dimensions: colors 0.30, spacings 0.30, typography 0.20, radii 0.10, shadows 0.10.

(4) CROSS-SESSION CONVERGENCE (CC), 0–1 (×100), weight 0.10:
  Run the SAME prompt N≥3 (recommend 5) independent times. Normalize each output (identifiers, whitespace, formatting — MANDATORY first, else naming-only diffs tank an otherwise-converged set). Extract styled value-selections per run. CC = Krippendorff's Alpha over the per-decision token/value selections across runs = (observed_agreement − expected_random_agreement)/(1 − expected_random_agreement). < 0.60 → flag for manual review (output too non-deterministic). Because N runs are costly, sample CC on a cadence (1–2 sprints/month), not every commit; accept single-run variance between samples.

CAVEAT baked into reporting: high composite is necessary but NOT sufficient for visual correctness — pair with screenshot/visual-regression for pixel fidelity; validate scores against human design review and retune weights if a high score meets poor UX feedback.
brief.convergenceProtocol:
The protocol is the system prompt AS a numbered, gated operational sequence (not advisory preamble), backed by harness tool-gating so it cannot be skipped:

STEP 0 — LOAD STATE: Read `design-system.json` + `decision-log.json` FIRST, before any generation. (Tool-gated: generation tools disabled until manifest is loaded this session.)
STEP 1 — RETRIEVE: Call `query_manifest({intent, category?, platform?})`. Score every candidate by cosine similarity to the new intent embedding. (Tool-gated: `create_component` FORBIDDEN unless `query_manifest` was called first in this session — the harness tool-call validator enforces ordering.)
STEP 2 — REUSE-vs-CREATE GATE: If top match ≥ 0.78 → REUSE the closest match (adapt via registered overrides only); log {matched-to-id, similarity, adaptation}. If < 0.78 → proceed to create, but record WHY the closest match was insufficient.
STEP 3 — ORDER OF OPERATIONS for any styling: match intent → reuse component → if styling needed, SNAP every value to the nearest `DS.*`/semantic token → only then create, and only as a first-class registered Style/Modifier/registry-item. NEVER emit a raw literal or an inline one-off variant.
STEP 4 — NAMING DETERMINISM: names follow the enforced template `{category}/{variant}/{modifiers}` (enum/dropdown selection, not free-form). IDs are `sha256(intent_keywords + signature_fingerprint + platform)[:16]` — content-derived, NOT uuid/sequential — so two independent agents building the same logical component compute the SAME id and the SAME file/name, which is what makes convergence mechanical rather than hoped-for.
STEP 5 — COLLISION → MERGE: Before appending, look up the computed id in `indices.byId`. If it exists, diff source/metadata and propose MERGE (union of source-locations) or an explicit VARIANT — never a silent fork.
STEP 6 — REGISTER LOOP: Auto-generate the manifest entry + decision-log entry, append, rebuild indices; require user confirmation before commit (default action = register; reject → roll back or mark experimental). No created artifact is ever invisible to the next session.
STEP 7 — EXCEPTIONS: Any deliberate off-scale value is logged in `decision-log.json` with a templated justification (platform-specific-override | temporary-workaround | legacy-compat | measured-perf). The audit path MUST query this log and surface the reason rather than auto-fixing.
STEP 8 — VARIANCE CONTROL: temperature 0.1–0.2 (0.0 for token/name references); for high-stakes shared components, multi-sample N=3–5 and return the output with highest semantic similarity to existing manifest entries.

Why this converges independent agents: identical content-hashed IDs + enforced naming template + mandatory same-manifest retrieval + reuse threshold means two agents on the same task, in different sessions, on different stacks, deterministically land on the same tokens, the same component id, and the same names — and the CC sub-metric measures exactly how well that holds.
openQuestions: Embedding determinism vs portability: deterministic IDs need a fixed, versioned embedding model for intent fingerprinting — which model, and how do we re-key the manifest when it changes without invalidating every existing ID? Do we fall back to keyword-hash IDs to stay model-independent?

Cross-platform reuse semantics: when a web Button and a SwiftUI button serve the same intent, is that one logical component with two platform implementations (shared id) or two ids linked by an intent cluster? This decides whether CR can credit cross-stack reuse and how the byPlatform index partitions.

Reuse threshold calibration: 0.78 is a borrowed default; it must be empirically tuned per design system's intent-cluster density. What labeled dataset / harness experiment do we run to set it, and should it be per-category (buttons tighter than layouts)?

Convergence weight tension: CC at 10% may under-incentivize the very property the framework exists to produce, yet raising it penalizes legitimately diverse outputs and is expensive (N runs). Should CC instead be a gate (fail < 0.60) rather than a weighted contributor?

Manifest authority & sync: if designers own tokens in Figma (Tokens Studio export) and engineers own the component registry in code, which half is canonical and how do we prevent the multi-source-of-truth drift the research explicitly warns against — one CI-enforced pivot file, or a merge step with conflict resolution?

Type-check guard coverage for TA: matching property-family to token $type is clean for color/dimension but ambiguous for composites (a typography token sets size+weight+leading at once) — how do we score partial application of a composite without false violations?

SwiftUI clone detection at scale: tree-edit distance over SwiftSyntax ASTs for the CR missed-opportunity metric is expensive on large view hierarchies; do we need a cheaper structural fingerprint, and what edit-distance threshold is right for SwiftUI's modifier-chain idiom vs React JSX?

Decision-log lifecycle: who resolves 'active' exceptions, and how do we prevent the log from becoming a dumping ground that quietly legitimizes drift (every literal 'justified') — does it need expiry dates or periodic review gates?
